chunks: So fear God as much as you can, and listen and obey, and spend in charity for your own good. He who is saved from his own avarice will be successful.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about saving oneself from avarice?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah At-Tahrim, this verse serves as a bridge between the preceding warnings to the Prophet's wives and the general command for all believers to cultivate Taqwa (God-consciousness) within their capacity. It emphasizes active obedience (Sam' wa Ta'ah) and voluntary charity (Infaq) as practical manifestations of faith, with Shia scholars highlighting that 'saving oneself from stinginess' refers to purifying the soul from the love of wealth, thereby ensuring true spiritual success (Falah).
